items.title: *** EDPS and University of Oxford's Institute for Ethics in AI establish collaboration ***
items.description: *** EDPS and University of Oxford's Institute for Ethics in AI establish collaboration *** The # EDPS and the University of Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI launched a new collaboration today 🤝. At the launch event, ‘Contemporary challenges, ancient wisdom: philosophy meets AI policy’, @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas underlined in his opening remarks that the digital transformation of our societies must remain anchored in public values, not driven solely by capability, scale or speed. Personal data, he noted, is connected to the person and must be judged against the standard of human dignity. The collaboration will be a structured exchange between academic research and institutional practice. It will draw on philosophical traditions, both western and eastern, to inform debates on AI governance, privacy and data protection, human agency, rights, power and human flourishing. The EDPS will pose questions arising from modern AI governance. The Institute will reply from the perspective of philosophers, in a series of written dialogues. items.title: *** IAPP Europe Congress 2026 - What is the lawful basis for AI? Navigating GDPR in a probabilistic world ***
items.description: *** IAPP Europe Congress 2026 - What is the lawful basis for AI? Navigating GDPR in a probabilistic world *** EDPS @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas took part in a panel at the IAPP Congress, on how GDPR applies to AI. He explained that each use of personal data, and each purpose behind it, has to be assessed on its own. Legitimate interest can be a valid basis for training AI in some cases, but it is never automatic. Organisations need to think it through and prepare a documented assessment before they start. He stressed that practical safeguards make the difference: using only the data that is needed, leaving out problematic sources, testing for risks and documenting choices. Individuals' rights must remain effective in practice; scraped special-category data raises additional Article 9 GDPR questions, even when collected incidentally. Challenges remain, and we all keep learning by doing and through exchanges. items.title: 🗣️ IAPP Europe Congress 2026
items.description: 🗣️ IAPP Europe Congress 2026 Protecting children online and respecting their fundamental rights go hand in hand. @ Supervisor Wiewiorowski spoke on the panel “Who Protects Child Rights Online? Protecting Children While Preserving Privacy” at the IAPP Europe Congress. He joined Leanda Barrington-Leach (5Rights Foundation), Cari Benn (Microsoft) and Moritz Hennemann (BfDI). Discussing the @ EUCommission Commission’s EU KIDS Act proposal, he stressed that age assurance alone does not address the underlying risks. He invited the co-legislators to assess which features genuinely require age assurance, and which risks safety-by-design measures benefiting all users can address. He also called for privacy-preserving solutions to be effectively available across the EU before the obligations apply. The Supervisor recalled the EDPS Opinion on the proposal, which recommends zero-knowledge proofs, several viable alternatives for age assurance, human intervention for contested decisions, and the exclusion of algorithmic age estimation. “Protection is about managing risks, not banning participation.” Wojciech Wiewiorowski added.
